subject: Mutual Trajectory Workbook: kickoff and template (draft)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@stellarus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Trajectory Workbook: kickoff and template (draft)

Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attached is a clean starter: the Mutual Trajectory Workbook (MAP-style) I drafted for Stellarus to map evaluation milestones, owners, success criteria, and a suggested close timeline.

Ask: can you review the Week0 / Pilot acceptance criteria and confirm the internal SMEs listed on the right? If we can lock owners this week, Marissa and I can finalize a 30–45 day tech + business pilot plan.

What’s included:
- Google Doc: Mutual_Trajectory_Workbook_v1.gdoc (link below) — sections: Goals, Success Metrics, Acceptance Criteria, Technical Validation Steps, Security/Compliance checklist.
- Slides: Week0-acceptance-deck.pptx — 2-slide summary for execs.

Draft timeline proposal (high level):
1) Week 0 — kickstart & infra access (SLA: 3 business days)
2) Week 1–3 — integration + model validation (security sign-off parallel)
3) Week 4–6 — acceptance testing and exec review
Goal: decision meeting at end of Week 6 about expansion.

Links:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBExAMPLE-workbook-draft

If that looks good, can you share the names for the data security reviewer, platform engineer, and the product sponsor? I’ll update the doc and share an editable copy.

Best,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0142

Attachment stubs: Mutual_Trajectory_Workbook_v1.gdoc (Google Doc link), Week0-acceptance-deck.pptx (pptx)

From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@stellarus.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: PartnershipOps <ops@stellarus.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 12:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mutual Trajectory Workbook: kickoff and template (draft)

Sean —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the deck. A few notes from our side:

1) Timeline: our execs pushed for a compressed evaluation to try to make a go/no-go decision in ~30 days rather than 45. That may be tight but doable if Week 1 is purely infra and we can parallelize security review.

2) Security/Compliance: we need to add a row for data residency & logging requirements — SOC 2 evidence will be requested by our compliance team. Can your security SMEs provide a high-level matrix (type of data stored, retention, access controls)?

3) Acceptance criteria: Product sponsor (myself), Platform lead (Maya Gonzalez — maya.g@stellarus.ai), Security reviewer (Samir Patel — samir.p@stellarus.ai). They want an explicit performance bar (p95 latency < 350ms for typical 512-token calls) and an accuracy sample set check (we can provide seed prompts).

I’m copying PartnershipOps so they can coordinate the calendar. If you can update the workbook with the requested rows and a 30-day option (minimal and ideal tracks), we’ll review and aim to sync next Tue.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Mutual Trajectory Workbook: kickoff and template (draft)

Sean / Monica —

I reviewed Alex's note. Quick internal suggestions before we update the doc:

- Add a compact "30-day sprint" column that collapses integration + validation into parallel streams. Call it "Rapid Track (30d)" vs "Standard Track (45d)".
- Security matrix: Monica, can you draft a one-page SOC2/retention summary our security team can sign off on? I'll insert it as an appendix.
- Performance bar: we can propose p95 < 350ms on 40% quantized model footprint — include a note where Redwood can run a comparator test.
- Owners: set Platform lead = monica_patel, Security contact = monica_patel (initial contact), Product sponsor = sean_gallagher (we'll be the Redwood PO for the pilot), Customer sponsor = Alex Harper.

Action items I will take:
1) Create the Rapid Track column in the workbook and seed milestone dates (ETA: EOD Thu).
2) Add an optional "exec decision" slide to the deck so Alex's exec sponsor can see a single-line ask.

Monica — any red flags?

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, PartnershipOps <ops@stellarus.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Trajectory Workbook: kickoff and template (draft)

Alex —

Thanks for the details and the owner names. We updated the workbook with a "Rapid Track (30d)" option and a security appendix stub. Link (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBExAMPLE-workbook-draft

Summary of updates: 
- Added rows: Data residency, Logging & Retention, SOC2 evidence checklist, Performance target (p95 < 350ms)
- Two tracks: Rapid (30d) and Standard (45d) with explicit milestone owners
- Week0 deliverables: infra access, test dataset ingest, security evidence packet
- Exec slide added to Week0 deck (Week0-acceptance-deck.pptx)

Next steps:
1) Can PartnershipOps propose 2x 30-min slots for Tue 09/29 to review?
2) Alex: confirm we can start Week0 infra access by Mon 10/4 if your platform team approves.

If those two yeses come back, we’ll treat this as a formal pilot kickoff and issue the MAP as the source-of-truth for milestone acceptance.

Best,
Sean
